as_of_cutoff: Public before 2022-10-01 only. Post-Oct-1 info deliberately excluded.
primary_source: Credit Suisse Financial Report 2Q22, SEC Form 6-K exhibit 99.1: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1053092/000137036822000068/cs-20220630_991.htm (published 2022-07-27)

liquidity_2Q22.note: LCR is Basel 30-day stress assumption; weighted retail+wholesale deposit runoff ~CHF 114bn over 30 days = ~29% of customer deposits is what the regulator assumes survivable.

deposit_insurance.source: esisuisse / Swiss Banking Act (search result: beobachter.ch; CS legal notes credit-suisse.com/legalnotes). Excludes Pillar 3a/vested benefits? (3a/vested covered separately CHF 100k extra). Covers deposits booked in Switzerland only.
deposit_insurance.reasoning: No CS disclosure of insured/uninsured split in 2Q22 (US-style disclosure absent). Proxies: (1) wealth-management-heavy: group AUM CHF 1,454bn vs deposits CHF 389bn; WM+IB+corporate wholesale deposits are largely above 100k. (2) LCR unweighted: retail+small-business deposits only CHF 158bn (41% of deposits); the remaining ~59% (>CHF 250bn) is corporate/institutional/financial/HNW operational deposits, essentially uninsured. (3) Within the 158bn retail/SME bucket, much is HNW (private banking) balances over 100k; assume at most ~35-50% of that value is under the limit => ~CHF 55-80bn insured at most, plus esisuisse only covers Swiss-booked deposits (non-Swiss clients uncovered). => insured ~8-25% of value; best 15%. Also 'insured' for sim: 100k covered per depositor, but behaviorally even insured depositors may be less runny.

geography_and_segments.deposits_by_region_disclosed: Not disclosed in 2Q22 report; use AUM regional split as proxy: ~55-60% Switzerland (CHF), ~15-20% EMEA ex-CH, ~15% APAC, ~8-10% Americas. Middle East not separately disclosed (inside EMEA); est 2-5% of AUM.
geography_and_segments.retail_vs_wealth_vs_corporate: Not disclosed as deposits. Proxy: Swiss Bank (retail + corporate/institutional) AUM CHF 544.5bn; Wealth Management AUM CHF 661.5bn; Asset Mgmt ~CHF 250bn. CHF 4Q21 Swiss Bank customer deposits roughly CHF 150-170bn (estimate, unverified).

additional_liquidity_within_1_week_est.SNB: Standing SNB facilities: intraday and Lombard-type repo with eligible collateral (SNB-eligible securities), plus SNB 'ECB-style' liquidity-shortage financing facility (LSFF, introduced as part of too-big-to-fail framework 2022 — law passed by Parliament, effective Jan 2023? treat as unavailable pre-Oct 2022) . Best estimate of usable emergency borrowing: CHF 50-100bn in Swiss collateral already in pool; sim default 15% of deposits (range 8-25%).
additional_liquidity_within_1_week_est.other_sources: Unencumbered non-HQLA securities & loan books pledgeable with Fed discount window / ECB (US and UK subs); reverse repo book (liquidity pool partially from reverse repo); est. CHF 30-60bn monetisable in a week at haircuts.
additional_liquidity_within_1_week_est.caveat: These are estimates, not disclosed. Liquidity is trapped by legal entity (CS Schweiz AG vs CS AG vs US IHC); Group HQLA overstates what is available to any one entity. HQLA of ~60% of deposits is the core, disclosed backstop.

situation_2022_09_30_public_context.ceo: Ulrich Koerner (CEO since Aug 2022 after Thomas Gottstein left); chairman Axel Lehmann
situation_2022_09_30_public_context.memo_content: Told employees not to confuse day-to-day share price with the bank's strong capital base and liquidity position; acknowledged 'critical moment' ahead of the strategic review; client talking points said widening CDS spreads should not be mistaken for capital or liquidity issues; promised updates to staff before the Oct 27 strategy update. Sources: cash.ch, Business Standard/Bloomberg, Fortune, Irish Times (all dated Oct 1-3 describing the memo).
situation_2022_09_30_public_context.planned_strategy_update: 2022-10-27 with 3Q22 earnings: restructuring with big changes to Investment Bank (expected capital raise, spin/shrink of IB, CS First Boston).

CDS_5y_bps.derivation: FT-cited 355 bps Monday Oct 3 'adding 105bp from Friday close' (post-Oct-1 datapoint used only to back out the Friday close)
CDS_5y_bps.caution: Fortune/Bloomberg quoted ~293 later. Range 230-260 for Sep 30 close; only 'approx. 250' is back-calculated, verify.

situation_2022_09_30_public_context.implied_default_probability_5y: ~23% per Fortune estimate (Oct 3) ; not a pre-Oct-1 figure
situation_2022_09_30_public_context.share_price: Near record lows around CHF 4 (Sep 30 close approx CHF 3.98-4.0, down ~55% YTD from ~CHF 8.7 at end of 2021; market cap roughly CHF 10-11bn). Approximate from memory/press, not verified from a source fetched.
situation_2022_09_30_public_context.ratings_context: DBRS downgraded CS AG LT issuer rating to BBB? (that was Oct 2022 -- excluded/not verified pre-Oct-1)
situation_2022_09_30_public_context.social_media_rumour_as_of_Oct1: Irish Times (Oct 3) says the bank was responding to 'rumours on social media about the bank's financial resilience' and a CDS spike during the previous week. In the week of Sep 26-30 Twitter/finance-Twitter posts compared CS to Lehman (CDS spike, 'Lehman moment' framing; Bloomberg reported CS Singapore/Asia and some clients asked about exposure); unverified details: I did not find a specific tweet pre-Oct-1. Weekend of Oct 1-2: Swiss press (e.g. Blick headline 'Anleger fürchten jetzt Konkurs', riskier than Greek banks) amplified; treat Blick as ~Oct 1-3.
situation_2022_09_30_public_context.other_pre_Oct1_context: Q2 2022 net loss CHF 1.59bn; AUM CHF 1,453.9bn (-10.9% YoY); Q2 net new assets -CHF 9.1bn total (WM -1.4, Swiss Bank -1.6, AM -6.1); CET1 ratio ~13.5% (CET1 capital CHF 37.0bn); 2021 Archegos and Greensill losses; earlier Sept 2022 CS statements of 'strong' capital; Koerner Sept 27 press mentions plan to take decisions earlier.

confidence_notes: Items 1,2 and AUM regions: high (primary source). Insured share, additional liquidity, deposit geography: estimates. Share price/CDS Sep 30: approximate; SNB LSFF note is uncertain.
